scheme_name: Providing Artificial Limbs and Other Appliances to Disabled BOC Workers
description:
The scheme for Providing Artificial Limbs and Other Appliances to Disabled BOC Workers is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing the quality of life for disabled workers in the country.

This scheme was launched in 2015 under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide artificial limbs and assistive devices to disabled workers who are part of the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

The scheme aims to ensure that these workers can regain their mobility and independence.

The government has set a measurable target of providing assistance to at least 10,000 disabled workers annually.

The scheme is designed to cover various types of disabilities including physical disabilities that hinder mobility.

Eligible beneficiaries include workers who are registered with the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

The age limit for eligibility under this scheme is set at 18 years and above.

There is no specific income criterion mentioned for eligibility.

However, preference is given to those who are economically weaker sections of society.

The application process for this scheme requires eligible workers to fill out a specific application form.

This form can be obtained from the local offices of the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

Applicants must provide proof of their disability through a medical certificate issued by a recognized medical authority.

Additionally, a copy of their identity proof such as an Aadhaar card or voter ID is required.

The application must also include a recent passport-sized photograph of the applicant.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by a committee formed under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

The committee will assess the applications based on the severity of the disability and the need for assistive devices.

The timeline for processing applications is typically around 30 days from the date of submission.

Once approved, the beneficiaries will be notified through their registered contact details.

The disbursement of artificial limbs and appliances is carried out in a phased manner.

Beneficiaries may receive their assistive devices within 60 days of approval.

The types of appliances provided under this scheme include prosthetic limbs, wheelchairs, and other mobility aids.

The government allocates a budget of approximately INR 50 crore annually for this scheme.

This budget is utilized for the procurement of high-quality artificial limbs and assistive devices.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of rehabilitation services for the beneficiaries.

Rehabilitation services include physiotherapy and counseling to help beneficiaries adapt to their new devices.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

The specific department responsible for the execution is the Directorate General of Employment.

Contact details for inquiries can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote inclusivity and support for persons with disabilities in India.

The government aims to reduce the barriers faced by disabled workers in the workforce.

Statistically, it is estimated that around 2.68 crore people in India are disabled.

Among these, a significant percentage are of working age and can benefit from this scheme.

The initiative aligns with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016.

This act emphasizes the need for equal opportunities and accessibility for disabled individuals.

The scheme also collaborates with various non-governmental organizations to enhance outreach.

NGOs play a crucial role in identifying eligible beneficiaries and assisting them with the application process.

The government regularly reviews the scheme to ensure its effectiveness and reach.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the services provided.

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform disabled workers about the availability of this scheme.

These campaigns are often held in collaboration with local community organizations.

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have regained mobility and independence.

Success stories are often highlighted in government publications to encourage more applications.

The government is committed to expanding the scope of this scheme in the coming years.

Future plans include increasing the budget allocation to meet rising demands.

The scheme also aims to introduce more advanced technologies in artificial limb manufacturing.

This will ensure that beneficiaries receive the best possible devices suited to their needs.

In conclusion, the scheme for Providing Artificial Limbs and Other Appliances to Disabled BOC Workers is a vital initiative that addresses the needs of disabled workers in India.

It not only provides essential mobility aids but also promotes rehabilitation and inclusivity.

The government’s commitment to this cause is reflected in the structured approach to application and disbursement.

With ongoing efforts to enhance the scheme, it is poised to make a significant impact on the lives of disabled workers across the country.
